Rashi on Nazir 38b:1:1.hebrew: ת"ק לא מדמי להו - לכל איסורי נזיר לשתיה, דאילו ענבים בכזית ויין ברביעית:
Rashi on Nazir 38b:1:1.english: The first tanna does not liken them - [namely,] all the prohibitions of a nazirite to drinking; for grapes [are measured] by an olive-bulk, and wine by a quarter-log.

Rashi on Nazir 38b:1:2.hebrew: כיון דכתיב וענבים לא יאכל - לכל מלתא הוא דאתא, דכשם שבזמן שהן ענבים מיחייב עליהן בכזית, אף כל איסור שבנזיר — בזמן שהן יין — בכזית:
Rashi on Nazir 38b:1:2.english: Since it is written: “Nor eat grapes” - It comes to [apply to] everything: that just as when they are grapes one is liable for them with an olive-bulk, so too every prohibition of a nazirite — when they are wine — [is] with an olive-bulk.

Rashi on Nazir 38b:2:1.english: That it is one type - For both fresh and dried are of the species of grapes.

Rashi on Nazir 38b:2:2.hebrew: והוא שתי שמות - לח ויבש, ואמרי להו: זג וחרצן:
Rashi on Nazir 38b:2:2.english: And it is two names - Fresh and dried; and some say: grape skin and grape seed.

Rashi on Nazir 38b:3:1.hebrew: לאיתויי חמרא חדתא ועינבי - שאע"פ שהן מין אחד, שהי' חדש מתוק כענבים — הואיל ושני שמות יש להן, חייב על כל אחת ואחת:
Rashi on Nazir 38b:3:1.english: To include new wine and grapes - For even though they are one species — as while it was new, [it was] sweet like grapes — since they have two [distinct] names, he is liable for each and every one.

Rashi on Nazir 38b:4:1.hebrew: אמר אביי אכל זג וחרצן לוקה שלש - אחת מכל אשר יעשה מגפן היין, ואחת על חרצנים, ואחת על זג — דלא יאכל אכולהו קאי:
Rashi on Nazir 38b:4:1.english: Abaye says: [If] he ate a grape skin and a grape seed, he is flogged three [times] - One [set of lashes is] from "anything that is made of the grapevine," and one for grape seeds, and one for a grape skin — for "he shall not eat" applies to all of them.

Rashi on Nazir 38b:4:2.hebrew: רבא אמר אכל זג וחרצן אינו לוקה אלא אחת - אפילו כי אכל זג וחרצן. אביי מתרץ מתניתין לטעמיה, דתני: וחייב על החרצנים בפני עצמן ועל הזגים — אפילו כשאוכל את שתיהן ביחד; וכן נמי למתניתא דתני: לחייב על זה בפני עצמו ועל זה בפני עצמו — ואפי' כשאוכל זג וחרצן בבת אחת. ורבא מתרץ לטעמיה: כגון דלא אכל אלא אחד מהם, דלא תימא עד שיאכל לחים ויבשים בהדי הדדי וחרצנים וזגים בהדדי, אלא אפי' לא אכל אלא לחים בלבד או יבשים בלבד — לוקה אחת. ולעולם אם אכל לחים ויבשים, או זג וחרצן — אינו חייב אלא אחת, ולא לאתויי חמרא חדתא ועינבי. ומתני' נמי תני: וחייב על היין בפני עצמו כו', דלא תימא עד דאכיל ליה לכולהו, אלא ודאי אכל חד מנהון לוקה; ומיהו כי אכיל נמי כולן יחד — אינו חייב אלא אחת:
Rashi on Nazir 38b:4:2.english: Rava says: If he ate a grape skin and a grape seed, he is flogged only once - [This means] even when he ate [both] a grape skin and a grape seed. Abaye explains the mishna according to his reasoning, as it teaches: “And he is liable for the grape seeds by themselves and for the grape skins” — [meaning] even when he eats both of them together; and likewise for the baraita that teaches: “To render [him] liable for this by itself and for that by itself” — [meaning] even when he eats a grape skin and a grape seed at the same time. But Rava explains according to his reasoning: [They are referring to a case] where he ate only one of them, so that you should not say [he is not liable] until he eats fresh and dried [grapes] together, or grape seeds and grape skins together; rather, even if he ate only fresh alone or dried alone, he is flogged once. And indeed, if he ate fresh and dried [grapes], or a grape skin and a grape seed, he is liable [to receive] only one [set of lashes], and [the baraita does] not [serve] to include new wine and grapes [to make him liable for both]. And the mishna also teaches: “And he is liable for wine by itself, etc.,” so that you should not say [he is not liable] until he consumes all of them; rather, certainly if he ate [just] one of them he is flogged. However, even when he consumes all of them together, he is liable only once.

Rashi on Nazir 38b:4:3.hebrew: ע"א: אינו לוקה אלא אחת - כשאוכל זג יחידי או חרצן, ואינו לוקה משום כל אשר יעשה. ולא צריך לשנויי לכל הני כדשנינן לעיל:
Rashi on Nazir 38b:4:3.english: Another interpretation: He is flogged only once - When he eats a grape skin alone or a [grape] seed, and he is not flogged on account of “anything that is made [of the grapevine].” And [he] does not need to resolve all those [sources] as we resolved [them] above.

Rashi on Nazir 38b:4:4.hebrew: דאין לוקין על לאו שבכללות - כגון האי, דעל כמה איסורי לית בהו אלא לאו חד:
Rashi on Nazir 38b:4:4.english: For one is not flogged for a general prohibition - Such as this [case], where for several forbidden items there is only one negative commandment concerning them.

Rashi on Nazir 38b:5:1.hebrew: ואם איתא - דלוקה משום "כל אשר יעשה מגפן היין", ליתני: לוקה שש:
Rashi on Nazir 38b:5:1.english: And if it is [so] - That he is flogged on account of “anything that is made of the grapevine,” let it teach: He is flogged six [times].

Rashi on Nazir 38b:7:1.english: He omitted “He shall not profane his word” - For he is also flogged for it:

Rashi on Nazir 38b:8:1.hebrew: והא שייר דבין הביניים - כדאמרי' לעיל (נזיר דף לד:): "ועד זג" — לאיתויי בין הביניים:
Rashi on Nazir 38b:8:1.english: But he omitted that which is in between - As we said above (Nazir 34b): "And unto the grape skin" — to include that which is in between [them].

Rashi on Nazir 38b:8:2.hebrew: אלא אמר רב פפא לא תנא מידי חמש - אלא לוקה סתם, ואיכא לתרוצי לאביי כי טעמיה ולרבא כי טעמיה, הואיל ולא נכתב ליה מניינא. וקמהדר הגמרא: ומאחר דלא תניא, מ"ט אותביה חמש:
Rashi on Nazir 38b:8:2.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said: [Rabbi Eliezer] did not teach anything of five - Rather, [the baraita taught] simply [that] he is flogged, and it can be explained according to Abaye in accordance with his reasoning, and according to Rava in accordance with his reasoning, since no tally was written in it. And the Gemara rejoins: And since it was not taught [as five], what is the reason that he [Rav Pappa] challenged him [Abaye] with "five"?

Tosafot on Nazir 38b:2:1.hebrew: ועל זה בעצמו - "לחים ויבשים" קרא יתירא הוא, ולכתוב "ענבים", והוי לחים ויבשים במשמע! אלא לחייב על זה בעצמו — שאם אכל ענבים לחים ויבשים בהתראה אחת שהתרו "אל תאכל ענבים", לוקה שתים; ואפי' הן מין אחד וטעם [אחד], כיון שהם שני שמות:
Tosafot on Nazir 38b:2:1.english: "And for that by itself" - "Fresh and dried" is a superfluous phrase in the verse; for let [the verse] write [simply] "grapes," and [both] fresh and dried would be implied! Rather, [it was stated] to render [him] liable for this by itself — that if one ate fresh grapes and dried [grapes] under a single warning, where they warned [him], "Do not eat grapes," he incurs two [sets of] lashes; and even though they are one species and [one] taste, since they are two [distinct] designations.

Tosafot on Nazir 38b:2:2.hebrew: ה"ג בגמרא: ומכאן אתה דן לכל איסורי נזיר, חמרא חדתי ועינבי - אע"פ שטעמם שוה, הואיל שהוא שני שמות — לוקה שתים. וא"ת: תיפוק ליה דחמרא חדתי וענבי כתיב בהדיא בקרא בתרי לאוין, דכתיב: "מיין ושכר יזיר", [ומתרגמינן]: "מחמר [חדת] ועתיק", וענבים כתיב! וי"ל: דאי מיזיר, ה"א חדתא כגון [ארבעה] יום, דאחר שלשה ימים שבצר אין טעמו כטעם ענבים; אבל יין [חדש] ממש, אימא לא מחייב אלא חדא; קמ"ל:
Tosafot on Nazir 38b:2:2.english: This is how we read in the Gemara: "And from here you derive with regard to all prohibitions of a nazirite: new wine and grapes" - Even though their taste is identical, since they are two [distinct] designations, he incurs two sets of lashes. And if you say: Let him derive it [from the fact] that new wine and grapes are written explicitly in the verse as two [separate] prohibitions, as it is written: "He shall abstain from wine and strong drink" (Numbers 6:3), and we translate [it in Targum Onkelos]: "from new and aged wine", and "grapes" is [also] written [in the verse]! And one can say: For if [we derived this only] from "He shall abstain", I would have said [that "new wine" refers to] new [wine of], for example, four days [old], for after three days from when he harvested, its taste is not like the taste of grapes; but [for] actual new wine, I would say he is liable for only one [set of lashes]. [Therefore,] it teaches us [that even with actual new wine, he incurs two sets of lashes].

Tosafot on Nazir 38b:4:1.hebrew: חרצן לוקה שתים - משום חרצן לא יאכל, ומשום מכל אשר יעשה מגפן היין:
Tosafot on Nazir 38b:4:1.english: [One who ate] a grape seed is flogged twice - On account of “[from grape] seeds... he shall not eat,” and on account of “anything that is made of the grapevine [he shall not eat]” (Numbers 6:4).

Tosafot on Nazir 38b:4:2.hebrew: אין לוקין על לאו שבכללות - דמכל אשר יעשה מגפן — כל מילי משמע, ואינו מפרש שום דבר:
Tosafot on Nazir 38b:4:2.english: One is not flogged for a general prohibition - For "from anything that is made of the grapevine" implies everything, and does not specify anything.

Tosafot on Nazir 38b:5:1.english: "They said to him: Do not drink" - That they warned him for each and every time that he wanted to drink.

Tosafot on Nazir 38b:5:2.hebrew: אכל ענבים לחים ויבשים וחרצנים וזגין - כלומר: כזית מכל אחד; וגם בסחט אשכול ענבים ושותה — לוקה ה': משום כזית ענבים לחים, וכזית יבשים, וכזית זגין, וכזית חרצנים, ומשום שותה יין:
Tosafot on Nazir 38b:5:2.english: "He ate fresh and dried grapes, and grape seeds and grape skins" - That is to say, an olive’s bulk of each one; and also [in the case where] he squeezed a cluster of grapes and drank, he is flogged five [times]: on account of an olive’s bulk of fresh grapes, an olive’s bulk of dried [grapes], an olive’s bulk of skins, an olive’s bulk of seeds, and on account of drinking wine.

Tosafot on Nazir 38b:5:3.hebrew: ולילקי שש מכל אשר וגו' - וא"ת: ולחשוב נמי התנא שכר וחומץ? וי"ל: דהא לאו שיורא הוא, אלא משייר מיניה; אבל בהנך דחשיב התנא — יש למנות כל המלקיות שבהם:
Tosafot on Nazir 38b:5:3.english: "And let him be flogged six [times], [one] for 'from all that' etc." - And if you say: Let the Tanna also enumerate [fermented] liquor and vinegar? And one can say: For this is not [a problematic] omission, but rather [the Tanna simply] omitted from it; however, regarding those [items] that the Tanna did enumerate, one must count all the [sets of] floggings that apply to them.

Tosafot on Nazir 38b:6:1.english: "He omitted bal yaḥel" - That he should also be flogged on account of bal yaḥel [“he shall not profane his word”].

Tosafot on Nazir 38b:7:1.hebrew: לאו שיורא - כי קתני, מילתא דליתא בשאר איסורין אלא בנזיר; אבל "בל יחל" שייך בשאר נדרים נמי. וא"ת: וכי נאמר כן כדי להקשות לאביי?! וי"ל: דקאמר הכי משום דלא תקשי לרבא: "מאי שייר דהאי שייר?" — דשייר "בל יחל", אומר הגמ' כן. דומיא דהכי מפרש ר"י בפ"ק דב"ק (דף טו.) גבי "אי משום חצי כופר לאו שיורא הוא":
Tosafot on Nazir 38b:7:1.english: "It is not an omission" - For when [the tanna] teaches, [he mentions only] a matter that does not apply to other prohibitions, but rather [only] to a nazirite; but "He shall not profane [his word]" applies to other vows as well. And if you say: Would [the Gemara] say this [merely] in order to raise a difficulty against Abaye?! And one can say: It says this so that it should not be difficult for Rava: "What [else] did he omit that he omitted this?" — [for if one were to say] that he omitted "He shall not profane [his word]," the Gemara says this [that it is not considered an omission]. The Ri explains similarly in the first chapter of Bava Kamma (15a) regarding "If it is due to half-ransom, that is not an omission."

Tosafot on Nazir 38b:8:1.hebrew: והא שייר בין הבינים - קושיא הוא למ"ד דלא יחל לא הוי שיור: אמאי שייר בין הבינים? וא"ת: התינח לפי' ר"ת דפירש (לעיל נזיר דף לה.) דבין הבינים היינו ענבים קטנים, דתנא באכילה, כדקתני "ואכל ענבים", בין גדולים בין קטנים משמע, ושייר [לאשכול] קטנים שלא מנאן — הלכך פריך שפיר; אלא לפירוש שני שפירש לעיל, דהביניים היינו [גוף] הענבים, הרי דתנא לא שייר כלום, דקתני "לוקה ה'", היינו משום ענבים לאו אחד! וי"ל, דגם לאותו פי' שייר לאו דידיה: דלאו דחיוב ענבים היינו כשאוכלן שלמים כדרך שאוכלים ענבים, אבל מלקט האוכל שביני וביני, שאין דרך לאכול כן, זהו לאו אחר של בין הביניים, והתנא שיירו. ואף על פי שמלשון התנא נמי משמע ששנה ואכל את הביניים דרך ליקוט, ד"אוכל ענבים" משמע בכל ענין, אפילו בליקוט — אפילו הכי לאו דידיה שייר, דאל"כ לילקי שש:
Tosafot on Nazir 38b:8:1.english: "But he omitted that which is in between" - This is a difficulty [raised] against the one who said that "he shall not profane [his word]" is not [considered] an omission: Why did [the Tanna] omit [the prohibition of] that which is in between? And if you say: This works out well according to the explanation of Rabbeinu Tam, who explained (above, Nazir 35a) that "that which is in between" refers to small grapes, so that [when] the Tanna taught regarding eating—as he teaches: "and he ate grapes"—it implies whether large or small, and he omitted [from the cluster] the small ones, as he did not enumerate them; therefore, [Ravina] objects well. However, according to the second explanation that was explained above, that "the between" refers to the [flesh of] the grapes—behold, the Tanna did not omit anything, for what he taught, "he is flogged five [times]," includes one negative commandment on account of grapes! And one can say that even according to that explanation, he omitted its [own distinct] negative commandment. For the negative commandment of liability for grapes is when he eats them whole, in the way people eat grapes; but if he picks out the food that is between [the seed and the skin]—since it is not the usual way to eat like that—this is another negative commandment of "that which is in between," and the Tanna omitted it. And even though from the wording of the Tanna it also implies that he taught [liability even if] he ate "the between" by way of picking it out—since "one who eats grapes" implies in any manner, even by picking—even so, he omitted its [separate] negative commandment; for if not so, let him be flogged six [times].

Tosafot on Nazir 38b:8:2.hebrew: לא תני מידי ה' - בלשון הברייתא ליכא ה', אלא לוקה סתם; ותוכל לפרש שש:
Tosafot on Nazir 38b:8:2.english: "He did not teach anything [about] five" - In the wording of the Baraita there is no [mention of] five; rather, [it states] "he is flogged" without qualification, and you can interpret [it as meaning] six.
